C1.departure_from_the_lowering_pattern: LOWERING-PLUGIN-1 L1 made `PlanBackend::identity()` a REQUIRED trait method, so the compiler proved every implementor stated one. C1 cannot: F3 holds the ContinuationProvider contract at nine methods. 'Every production provider states an identity' is therefore witnessed by enumeration (two production impls at baseline, both covered) rather than by the type system. C2 closes the gap structurally: a provider becomes selectable only through a factory, and a factory states its identity to register.

C2.name: continuation registry
what_landed: `exec/continuation_registry.rs`: `ContinuationFactory` (identity, declared `regions()`, `validate_config` defaulting to 'takes no options', `build` → `BoxedContinuation = Box<dyn ContinuationProvider + Send>`); `ContinuationRegistry` — a value, `Clone`, no static and no default; `register` refuses invalid and duplicate identities; `select(identity, config, geometry)` refuses unregistered (naming what is), refused configuration, and the first layer whose region is not declared, all BEFORE anything is built; `SelectedContinuation` carries the authority and builds a fresh provider per call.

`exec/continuation_authority.rs`: `ContinuationConfig` (key=value, key order, shape refusals), `ConfigDigest` = `sha256:` over a domain tag, the identity and the canonical form, and `ContinuationAuthority { identity, config_digest }` — serde, the pair C4 carries.
`ContinuationRegion { Kv, LatentKv, Recurrent, KvAndRecurrent }` with `required_by(&LayerContinuationGeometry)`; refusal texts reuse `continuation::region_name`, the plan's one vocabulary.

Built-in factories beside their providers: `RowFactory` (exec/kv.rs), `CanonicalFactory` and `shipped_continuations()` — a fresh registry value per call (larql-kv/src/vindex3/registry.rs). Both declare all four regions and take no options.
No call site migrated: C2 must not change graph semantics, and it changes none. Migration is C3.

witnesses.exec/tests/continuation_registry.rs (12): configuration shape and key order; digest pinned to values computed OUTSIDE the crate (Python hashlib over the documented canonical form); digest moves with value, key set, family and revision but not key order; authority's two fields independent; registration refusals; unregistered names the registry; configuration refused by the provider that reads it; hybrid plan refused at selection naming layer 2 / recurrent (F5); KV + Recurrent separately do not hold a conv-QKV layer; stateless layers ask nothing; every build is a fresh provider driven through the full hybrid contract as a trait object
witnesses.larql-kv shipped_continuations_is_a_fres: two identities in order, registering into one leaves the next at two, both select and build against the miniature fixture plan's real geometry
witnesses.mutation control: disabling the region check in `select` (`if false && …`) turned exactly the two F5 witnesses red (10 passed, 2 failed); restored and re-verified

departures_from_the_forecast: The frozen boundary lists `Stateless` among the capability vocabulary. It is NOT a capability here: a stateless layer asks nothing of a provider, so declaring it would be a capability that can never be absent — an enum value no provider could meaningfully decline, which the same boundary forbids. Selection skips stateless layers; `a_stateless_layer_asks_nothing_of_a_provider` pins that a provider declaring nothing accepts an all-stateless plan.

The config digest covers the identity as well as the configuration (as frozen). Consequence for C4: the two authority fields are compared separately, identity first, so a changed identity reports as a provider/revision refusal and never as a configuration mismatch.
